title: Donut Binary — Secondary Segment Color & Primary-Only Labeling

complexity.rationale: The 2-segment (isBoolean) donut already exists and mostly works - this corrects two specific, well-documented gaps against the donut-binary skill, each a single coordinated site: forcing the secondary segment's fill to secondary-gray (adapting the same kind of test-expression color-swap pattern already speced for donut-emphasize/Line's primarySeries), and changing SegmentLabel's isBoolean handling from a full early-return to a primary-row-only filter. No open design questions - the donut-binary skill is short and unambiguous, and both changes are the same already-precedented shape.

summary: The existing isBoolean (2-segment binary) donut variant has two gaps against the documented donut-binary design. First, the secondary/complementary segment's arc always renders via the normal categorical color scale - it's never forced to chart.donut.color.secondary-gray as the design requires, confirmed by getArcMark (donutUtils.ts:48-76) having no isBoolean handling at all. Second, direct labels (SegmentLabel) are disabled entirely for isBoolean donuts (`if (isBoolean) return [];` in getSegmentLabelMarks) rather than being restricted to just the primary segment as the design intends ('Only the primary segment is labeled'). packages/vega-spec-builder (s1) has the identical gap, but per project direction this work is s2-only - s1 is intentionally left unchanged.
requirements: When isBoolean is true, the secondary (non-primary) segment's arc fill must always be chart.donut.color.secondary-gray (#C6C6C6/gray-400), overriding the normal categorical color-scale rule - regardless of what color the data's second row would otherwise map to via the color domain.
When isBoolean is true, the primary segment continues to render its own normal categorical color, unaffected.

The primary segment is the first data point, consistent with isBoolean's existing documented convention ('displays the first datapoint as a percent') - the secondary segment is the complementary/remaining share.
When isBoolean is true, direct labels (SegmentLabel) must render for the primary segment only, not be disabled entirely as they are today - the secondary segment stays unlabeled.
No separate swatch legend for binary donuts - already correct today (DonutSummary in the center hole already serves this role); no change needed here.

designTokens.usage: Fixed fill for the secondary/complementary segment of a binary donut, regardless of the data's own color-domain mapping.

edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Per donut-benchmark, the primary segment's color can already switch to a sentiment color when Benchmark+Semantic is set - confirm the secondary segment still renders secondary-gray in that combination, unaffected by the primary segment's sentiment override.

Emphasize's gray-swap and binary's forced secondary-gray could look redundant/conflicting on a 2-segment donut - confirm expected behavior when both are configured together (same open concern already flagged in donut-emphasize's edge cases).

edgeCases.case: User-supplied custom color scale/domain where the secondary row has its own explicit categorical color
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The secondary-gray override must always win for isBoolean donuts, regardless of what the color domain would otherwise assign to that row.

edgeCases.case: SegmentLabel with value/percent shown on the primary segment
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Existing percent/value formatting logic (getSegmentLabelValueText) continues to work unchanged - it simply now actually renders for isBoolean donuts, where previously it was suppressed entirely.

Both gaps are confirmed identical in packages/vega-spec-builder (s1) - its donutUtils.ts has no isBoolean handling in its arc fill either, and its segmentLabelUtils.ts has the identical `if (isBoolean) return [];` early-return - but per project direction this work is s2-only; s1 is intentionally left unchanged, not a gap to track here.

crossCutting.notes: requiresNewSignalOrScale is false - this is a new production rule on the existing arc fill encode (a static isBoolean/primary-row test expression, no new signal or scale), and a filter change to an existing function's early-return, not new reactive state. requiresS1S2Parity is false: per project direction, this work is scoped to s2 only. packages/vega-spec-builder (s1) has the identical gap (no isBoolean handling in getArcMark, same `if (isBoolean) return [];` gate in segmentLabelUtils.ts), but s1 is intentionally left unchanged, not treated as a parity gap.

implementationPlan.change: In getArcMark, add isBoolean to the destructured options and extend the fill encode with a test expression: when isBoolean and the row is not the primary (first) data point, use secondary-gray; otherwise use the existing getColorProductionRule(color, colorScheme) result.
In getSegmentLabelMarks, change the isBoolean handling from `if (isBoolean) return [];` to filtering the label's data source to the primary row only, rather than suppressing labels entirely.
Add tests for the secondary-gray override and the primary-only label filtering.
Add or update a story exercising isBoolean with a SegmentLabel child, confirming the primary segment shows its category color + label and the secondary segment renders gray and unlabeled.
